plan.title: Who Moved My Cheese? - The Parable Begins
plan.summary: A grounded manga adaptation of the opening slice of Who Moved My Cheese?, covering the book's introduction, the Chicago gathering that frames the story, the four characters' discovery of Cheese Station C, the moment the cheese disappears, Hem's denial, and Haw's first steps into the unknown Maze.

item.book_essence: The book introduces itself as a simple parable that reveals profound truths about change through four characters who live in a Maze and look for Cheese to nourish them and make them happy.
item.dramatization: A title spread frames the story as a timeless parable, with the four characters introduced as inhabitants of an unseen Maze whose Cheese is what they want in life.

item: Title spread with a stylized maze illustration
Four small silhouettes framed against a maze outline
Glossary panel naming Sniff, Scurry, Hem, and Haw
The story is a simple parable that reveals profound truths about change
Four characters live in a Maze looking for Cheese to nourish them and make them happy
Two characters are mice named Sniff and Scurry
Two are little people named Hem and Haw, beings the size of mice who look and act a lot like people
Cheese is a metaphor for what you want to have in life
The Maze is where you look for what you want
The reading-time estimate can be omitted
The list of sub-sections can be omitted

item.book_essence: Former classmates gather for lunch in Chicago after their high school reunion and discover they all struggle with unexpected change, leading Michael to share a story called Who Moved My Cheese?
item.dramatization: A medium shot of friends around a lunch table transitions to close-ups of Angela, Nathan, Carlos, and Michael as resistance to change surfaces and the title is named.

item: Medium shot of classmates around a lunch table
Close-up of Angela saying life turned out differently than she thought
Close-up of Michael announcing the story's title
Several former classmates gather for lunch in Chicago after a high school reunion
Angela notes that life turned out differently than she thought
Nathan notes that people do not want to change when things change
Carlos admits he resists change because he is afraid of it
Michael shares a story that changed how he looked at change
Michael tells the group the story is called Who Moved My Cheese?

item.book_essence: Four characters are introduced: mice Sniff and Scurry with simple brains and good instincts, and little people Hem and Haw with complex brains and many beliefs and emotions, all searching the Maze for cheese.
item.dramatization: An establishing shot of the Maze introduces each character in turn, with a visual cue distinguishing the simple trial-and-error of the mice from the complex belief-driven approach of the little people.

item: Wide establishing shot of the Maze corridors and chambers
Sniff and Scurry putting on running shoes in their simple home
Hem and Haw in jogging suits with thought-bubble overlays of capital-C Cheese
Four characters run through a Maze looking for cheese to nourish them and make them happy
Sniff and Scurry are mice who possess simple brains and good instincts
Hem and Haw are little people whose complex brains are filled with many beliefs and emotions
Sniff and Scurry use a simple trial-and-error method of finding cheese
Hem and Haw use complex brains to develop more sophisticated methods
The four characters represent the simple and the complex parts of ourselves, regardless of age, gender, race, or nationality

item.book_essence: All four characters discover cheese at Cheese Station C and settle into routines, with the mice keeping running shoes handy and the little people becoming comfortable enough to decorate the walls.
item.dramatization: A wide shot of a cheese-filled Cheese Station C transitions to a calmer beat showing the routines: mice tying shoes around their necks and little people hanging up jogging suits to decorate the walls with sayings and cheese drawings.

Mice tying running shoes around their necks
Little people hanging up jogging suits and decorating walls with cheese drawings

Sniff and Scurry keep their running shoes tied together and hung around their necks for quick access
Hem and Haw hang up their jogging suits, put away their running shoes, and put on slippers
Hem declares there is enough Cheese to last them forever
Hem and Haw decorate the walls with sayings and pictures of cheese

item.book_essence: The cheese at Cheese Station C is gone; Sniff and Scurry had been watching the supply shrink and quickly put on their running shoes, while Hem yells and Haw freezes in disbelief.
item.dramatization: An empty cheese station is revealed on a page turn, with the mice already lacing up their running shoes; Hem shouts in a close-up while Haw stands frozen.

Mice lacing running shoes and looking out into the Maze
Hem yelling 'Who moved my Cheese?' in close-up
Haw frozen in disbelief, hands at sides

The mice had noticed the supply getting smaller and were prepared for the inevitable
The mice remove their running shoes from around their necks, put them on, and lace them up
Hem yells 'No Cheese?' and 'Who moved my Cheese?'
Haw shakes his head and stands frozen with shock
Hem denies and resists change because he fears it will lead to something worse

item.book_essence: Hem insists the cheese must still be there and hammers at the wall in futility while believing the mice know nothing, but Haw begins to imagine finding New Cheese and feels drawn to the Maze.
item.dramatization: A medium shot of Hem and Haw at the empty station shows denial turning to anger; a quiet close-up of Haw shows him imagining new cheese and feeling drawn to the Maze.

item.book_essence: Haw laughs at his own folly, retrieves the running shoes, decides it is time to find New Cheese, writes a message on the wall for Hem, and announces 'It's Maze time!' before stepping into the unknown.
item.dramatization: Haw is shown laughing at himself, lacing up the running shoes, writing a saying on the wall for Hem, and stepping into an unfamiliar corridor with a determined but weak posture.

item.book_essence: Haw ventures into parts of the Maze where he had never been, finds only small amounts of cheese that do not last, and admits he is fearful of going on alone, asking himself what he would do if he were not afraid.
item.dramatization: Haw is shown alone in a vast maze corridor, weak and hesitant, with a final close-up on his question as the page turns.

plan.ending_state: Haw stands alone at the threshold of an unfamiliar corridor, weak from hunger but having chosen to move and adapt, asking himself what he would do if he were not afraid, while Hem remains behind at the empty Cheese Station C and Sniff and Scurry are already far ahead in the Maze pursuing new cheese.
